# PieChartElement

**Class:** `UltraCanvasPieChartElement` · **Group:** [Charts](../Groups/Charts.md) · **Header:** [`UltraCanvas/include/Plugins/Charts/UltraCanvasPieChart.h`](../../../UltraCanvas/include/Plugins/Charts/UltraCanvasPieChart.h) · `#include "Plugins/Charts/UltraCanvasPieChart.h"`

**Inherits:** [`UltraCanvasChartElementBase`](UltraCanvasChartElementBase.md) → [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md) → `Element`

## What it is for

Parts of a whole: pie, donut, 3D pie

## Creating it

Factory functions (the usual way - every element is held in a `std::shared_ptr`):

```cpp
std::shared_ptr<UltraCanvasPieChartElement> CreatePieChartElement( const std::string& id, int x, int y, int w, int h);
```

Constructors:

```cpp
UltraCanvasPieChartElement(const std::string& id, int x, int y, int w, int h);
```

The first string argument is always the element's **identifier**, never its text (see [Core concepts](../Core-Concepts.md#identifiers)).

## Callbacks

Assign a lambda to the member (or call the setter). Capture the element and its parents **raw**, never as a `shared_ptr` - see [Events and callbacks](../Events-and-Callbacks.md#ownership).

| Callback | Signature | When it fires |
|---|---|---|
| `SetPercentageFormatter()` | `void SetPercentageFormatter(std::function<std::string(double pct)> f)` | Takes a callback. |
| `SetValueFormatter()` | `void SetValueFormatter(std::function<std::string(double v)> f)` | Takes a callback. |
| `onSliceClick` | `std::function<void(size_t)> onSliceClick` | Both receive the slice's data-source index. |
| `onSliceHover` | `std::function<void(size_t)> onSliceHover` | _Slice hover_ |

**Inherited callbacks:**

- from [`UltraCanvasChartElementBase`](UltraCanvasChartElementBase.md): `SetCustomTooltipGenerator`
- from [`UltraCanvasUIElement`](UltraCanvasUIElement.md): `eventCallback`, `onPopupAboutToClose`, `onPopupClosed`, `onPopupOpened`, `SetEventCallback`

| `UpdateRenderingCache` | `void UpdateRenderingCache() override` | The slices are cut from the data, so whatever invalidates the base cache - a new data source above all - invalidates them too. Without this a chart handed fresh data kept drawing the old slices (with the new centre text), since only the pie's own setters knew to drop them. |
